wanted: For the temple to actually do something with the fragment - seal it, name it, end the bell
For the acolyte who said 'I hope you are a slow looker' to prove that hope was earned
To look up at the thing above the city and have it acknowledge me back, some answer that the measuring could be stopped
For P'taxx to know what this was; for at least one adult in the story to stop blocking doorways
feared: That the fragment was never an object but a test, and that choosing the temple had been the test passing itself to me
That the thing above the city was counting my heartbeats and every scene I lingered in was just making the number smaller
That 'your name burning across the lid' was not a warning but a verdict, and that the final widening to the whole city meant I had already lost and the city was just collateral
attention_intensified: 022b: the name burned across the iron lid - 'Not temple script. Not the script from P'taxx's books. / Your name.' - the first time the threat named me directly and personally, and the acolyte's whispered 'That is impossible' made the impossible feel witnessed by someone I'd started to trust
attention_weakened: 022b: the long 'is' chain after 'The Lattice is waiting.' ('The reliquary is still open. The name is still burning. ... and the reading is the one the city is watching.') - the restatement loop drained the tension the name-burn had just built; I was re-reading the same state six times and my pulse was flat by the last line
confused: 021b: the scene is titled 'The Walk to the Shop' but we were walking to the temple; P'taxx is inside before anyone opens the door, and the acolyte's 'You sent him to me' is never answered or resolved; the walk is essentially skipped
021b: quote-mark style flips mid-scene (curly for the acolyte, straight for the protagonist) - reads like two different passes of the text
021b: the protagonist suddenly knows 'it's measuring... counting down... to me looking up' - the fragment never said that on this route; the 'counting down' framing appears out of nowhere
022: the 'choices' revelation ('Roots. No. Roads. No. Choices.') felt like a thesis being announced rather than experienced
022b: 'They do not look as though they were in the square when the bell first rang' - but they were in the square in 020; I could not reconcile which version of the square was canonical
residue: 'It measures looking away. It has no word for looking back.' kept circling after the last scene - the whole route was one long act of refusing to look away, and the story never let me find out what happens to a cat that never looks away
The name on the iron lid and every cat in Faelspire stopping at once to listen to something I can no longer hear - a defeat that is also a widening, the opposite of closure
The acolyte's 'I hope you are a slow looker' - the only line in the route that sounded like a person
